messages.content: What is the common ancestor of lion and zebra?

message.content:
The last common ancestor of a lion (Panthera leo) and a zebra (Equus quagga) is the same ancestor that gave rise to all placental mammals (Eutheria).  
That ancestor was a small, insect‑eating mammal that lived roughly 100–120 million years ago, before the lineages that would become the carnivores (lion’s lineage) and the odd‑toed ungulates (zebra’s lineage) split apart.
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "What is the common ancestor of lion and zebra?" They want a biological answer. The lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga) are both mammals, but belong to different orders: lions are Carnivora, zebras are Perissodactyla. Their common ancestor would be at the level of the last common ancestor of all placental mammals? Actually, lion and zebra diverged earlier. The last common ancestor of all placental mammals is the ancestor of all eutherians. But maybe they want the last common ancestor of the two species: that would be the last common ancestor of the families Felidae and Equidae, which is the ancestor of the order Carnivora and Perissodactyla. That would be the ancestor of the clade that includes all placental mammals except monotremes and marsupials? Wait, monotremes are egg-laying mammals; marsupials are separate. Placental mammals diverged from marsupials around 160 million years ago. The last common ancestor of carnivores and perissodactyls would be the ancestor of the clade that includes all placental mammals except monotremes? Actually, monotremes diverged earlier. So the last common ancestor of lion and zebra is the last common ancestor of all placental mammals, which lived about 100-120 million years ago. But if we want more specific: the last common ancestor of the two species is the ancestor of the clade that includes all placental mammals, which is the ancestor of the group called Eutheria. That ancestor would have been a small, insectivorous mammal.

Alternatively, we could say the last common ancestor of lion and zebra is the last common ancestor of the orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla, which is the ancestor of the clade that includes all placental mammals except monotremes. That ancestor lived around 100 million years ago.

Thus answer: the last common ancestor of lion and zebra is the last common ancestor of all placental mammals, a small insectivorous mammal that lived ~100-120 million years ago. Or we can mention the ancestor of the clade that includes all eutherian mammals.

We should provide a concise answer. No need to call the function.
